arguments.report:
FIXED: Interval.fromISO with Settings.throwOnInvalid = true.

CAUSE
In src/interval.js `fromISO`, both halves were eagerly parsed as DateTimes:
  const start = DateTime.fromISO(s, opts), end = DateTime.fromISO(e, opts);
When one half is a duration (e.g. "PT5H30M"), DateTime.fromISO returns an invalid DateTime, but with Settings.throwOnInvalid = true DateTime.invalid() throws InvalidDateTimeError (src/datetime.js:860) instead of returning an invalid DateTime, so the code never reached the Duration branch. Same for the duration-first form.

CHANGES (only file touched: /luxon/src/interval.js; no test files modified — `git status --short` shows only ` M src/interval.js`)
1. Added module-level helper (lines ~9-17):
   function tryParseDuration(text, opts) { try { return Duration.fromISO(text, opts); } catch (err) { return null; } }
2. `Interval.fromISO` (lines ~144-177): each `DateTime.fromISO` is now wrapped in try/catch, recording `startIsValid` / `endIsValid` (a thrown error => "not valid"), and the branch logic uses those booleans. The Duration parses now go through `tryParseDuration` and are guarded with `dur && dur.isValid`.
   - DateTime try/catch is the core fix (matches the reported cause).
   - The Duration try/catch is the same class of bug (Duration.invalid() also throws under throwOnInvalid, src/duration.js:282): without it, `Interval.fromISO("R5/2008-03-01T13:00:00Z/P1Y2M10DT2H30M")` (in the existing badInputs list) leaked an InvalidDurationError instead of reaching `Interval.invalid(...)`. With it, every genuinely unparsable input reaches the final `Interval.invalid("unparsable", ...)`, so with throwOnInvalid=true it throws InvalidIntervalError as required.
Behavior with throwOnInvalid=false is unchanged (invalid parses return invalid objects, no throws).

VERIFICATION
- Baseline before change: `npx jest test/interval` => 9 suites / 127 tests passed. `npx jest` => 54 passed, 1 failed (test/datetime/toFormat.test.js, 2 failures: 'FFF'/'FFFF' fr locale ICU f

arguments.text: Bug #5 is fixed and verified. Cause: `padStart` in src/impl/util.js padded the whole string form of the number, so the leading `-` counted as one of the digits (`padStart(-1, 4)` → `"00-1"`). Fix: pad the magnitude and prepend the sign separately, matching Intl's `minimumIntegerDigits` semantics. Now `-1` → `-0001-01-01`, `-10` → `-0010-01-01`, `-100` → `-0100-01-01`, `-999` → `-0999-01-01` (and toISO/toISOWeekDate/toFormat/toRFC2822/Interval output all follow). A sweep of years -12345…118040 across 39 format tokens plus all ISO/JSON/RFC/HTTP outputs shows only negative-year lines changed — year 0 and every positive year are byte-identical. Full suite: 892 passed / 2 failed, the same 2 pre-existing French-ICU `toFormat` failures as before the fix.

arguments.text: Bug #4 is fixed and verified. Cause: the conversion matrices in src/duration.js were incomplete — `casualMatrix.years` had no `quarters` entry and `casualMatrix.quarters` had no `seconds` entry (same gap in `accurateMatrix.years`), so `convert()` read `undefined` and produced NaN. Fix: added the three missing entries (`years.quarters: 4`, `quarters.seconds: 91*24*60*60`), consistent with the surrounding matrix. Now `{years:1,quarters:2}` → `{years:1,quarters:2}` with `as("years")` → 1.5, `{quarters:1,seconds:2}` no longer NaN, and `{quarters:1}.as("seconds")` → 7862400 (was silently 0). An exhaustive 9×9 unit-pair sweep × {casual, longterm} shows no NaN and no missing matrix entries; a 744-output before/after snapshot diffed to only the 18 previously-NaN/silently-0 entries. Duration suite 114/114 passing; full suite unchanged (892 passed, same 2 pre-existing French-ICU toFormat failures).

arguments.text: Bug #6 is fixed and verified. Cause: `FixedOffsetZone` hard-coded `get isValid() { return true; }`, so a non-numeric offset like `"CDT"` was accepted; DateTime only emits `"unsupported zone"` when `!zone.isValid`, so the bogus zone slipped through and the DateTime ended up invalid with reason `"invalid input"` instead. Fix (src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js): `isValid` now returns `isNumber(this.fixed)`. Now `new FixedOffsetZone("CDT").isValid === false`, and `DateTime.fromMillis(0, { zone })` is invalid with reason `"unsupported zone"` (explanation: `the zone "UTC-NaN" is not supported`). All valid offsets are unchanged (`utcInstance`, `instance(360)` → "UTC+6", `instance(-390)` → "UTC-6:30", `parseSpecifier("UTC+6")`, zone strings "utc"/"GMT"/"Etc/GMT+5", fromISO/fromRFC2822/fromFormat offset parsing). Zones suite 32/32 passing; full suite unchanged (892 passed, same 2 pre-existing French-ICU toFormat failures).
